basis: Statements are drawn ONLY from the classified evidence records in the V3 correction (R394 retrieval, R394/p07_evidence/) and the package's own governing model. No novelty or patentability conclusion is drawn.
what_is_already_known: Multi-lumen ventricular drainage catheters exist: a 2010 patent-shaped record describes a ventricular drainage catheter with at least two lumens at the distal end and one slit and aperture per lumen; dual-lumen ventricular catheter systems are in clinical use for combined continuous drainage and irrigation (PMID 38468682, 2024); dual-lumen intrathecal catheters are used in a current prospective trial for extracorporeal CSF filtration (PILLAR-XT, PMID 40745075, 2025). Catheter architecture demonstrably changes outflow resistance and occlusion behavior in vitro (16 design variations, blood-inoculated CSF; PMID 39944477, 2025), alternative anti-occlusion architectures are under active assessment (multilayered fibrous webs, PMID 41616221), and approximately 40% of shunts fail within two years, primarily from catheter occlusion. Programmable valve-based flow control is the incumbent flow-control art.
what_is_different: The P-07 concept is a permanently open, lower-conductance floor lumen running the full catheter length in parallel with the primary lumen, providing passive drainage redundancy against primary-lumen obstruction in a chronic shunt. The known dual- and multi-lumen systems use their lumens for different functions (drainage plus irrigation, aspiration plus return) or as distal-end parallel tips; none is documented as a parallel-redundancy conductance floor for obstruction immunity in a chronic shunt.
why_the_difference_matters: The failure mode being addressed (obstruction-driven revision) requires the second path to remain patent when the first obstructs — a redundancy function, not an irrigation or return function. The difference matters only if the floor lumen's obstruction susceptibility differs from the primary lumen's; if both obstruct from the same cause (common-cause failure), the redundancy is void. That differential susceptibility is exactly the unresolved kill condition.
what_evidence_supports_it: The parallel-conductance behavior is modelled (Hagen-Poiseuille and the parallel-sum governing equations, with recorded units and dimensional validation states in EQUATION_REGISTRY.json); the architecture-versus-occlusion relationship is evidenced in vitro for ventricular catheters generally (PMID 39944477); multi-lumen catheter manufacturability is established by clinical deployment (PMID 38468682, PMID 40745075). No retrieved evidence yet shows differential obstruction immunity of parallel lumens.
what_remains_unknown: Whether the floor lumen is genuinely immune — or differentially susceptible — to the same obstruction mechanism as the primary lumen (the common-cause kill condition; untested in the retrieved literature and the package's decisive experiment target); the achievable G_floor/G_primary ratio under multi-lumen extrusion tolerances; the clinically safe Q_min; and whether the 2010 multi-lumen ventricular drainage catheter prior art anticipates the specific parallel-redundancy function, which is a legal determination this record does not draw.
